text: Faculty of Science and Humanities academic calendar 2026-27, odd semester: I year UG and PG - course enrolment 29 June 2026, classes commence 8 July 2026, Internal Assessment I (cycle test) 11 Aug 2026, Internal Assessment II 21 Sept 2026, model exam 8 Oct 2026, university practical exam 16 Oct 2026, last working day 16 Oct 2026, university theory exams start 2 Nov 2026. II and III year UG and II year PG (semester 3) - enrolment 15 June, classes 24 June 2026, cycle test I 4 Aug, cycle test II 15 Sept, model exam 6 Oct, practicals 14 Oct, theory exams from 2 Nov 2026.

Faculty of Science and Humanities academic calendar 2026-27, even semester (semesters 2 and 4): course enrolment 20 Nov 2026, classes commence 30 Nov 2026, cycle test I 19 Jan 2027, cycle test II 2 Mar 2027, model exam 24 Mar 2027, last working day 2 Apr 2027, end-semester practicals from 5 Apr 2027, detention list submission 5 Apr 2027, internal mark submission 9 Apr 2027, end-semester theory exams from 20 Apr 2027.

The Engineering and Technology (CET) academic schedule for July 2026 - June 2027, for UG and PG, is published on the Students page as an official PDF (Overall Academic Schedule). It lists semester enrolment, classes, cycle tests, model exams and tentative university theory exam dates. Open https://www.srmist.edu.in/students/cet-academic-schedule-2026-2027-ug-pg/ for the exact dates of your year.

A semester at SRMIST typically has: course enrolment, classes, two cycle tests (Internal Assessment I and II), a model practical and model theory exam, end-semester practical exams, end-semester theory exams and then central valuation. Saturdays can be working days with a rotating five-day 'day order' system (Day Order I to V), so a Saturday may follow a weekday timetable.

SRMIST examination policy: students must keep the minimum attendance required by their regulations to be eligible for exams; a student can be detained from exams for not meeting attendance or internal assessment criteria. Hall tickets must be obtained and shown for admission to every exam, and a lost hall ticket must be replaced through the Controller of Examinations. Exam registration and fees must be paid before the deadline.

Revaluation: results can be sent for review, revaluation and retotalling within 7 days of the result declaration. These are not permitted for practical examinations. Makeup exams may be offered to students who miss an exam for a valid reason, with prior notification, and a student who misses an exam because of illness can appeal with a medical certificate.

Exam malpractice: students may not carry unauthorised materials or electronic devices into exams. Malpractice leads to severe penalties - the policy says it can cancel all subjects written in that semester and, in serious cases, lead to expulsion. Candidature can also be cancelled if a student is found ineligible before or after hall tickets are issued. Exam timetables are at https://www.srmist.edu.in/controller-of-examinations/examination-time-tables/

SRMIST library timings: Central Library is open Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. and Saturday-Sunday 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. The Architecture Library and School of Law Library are open Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed on weekends. The Circulation Counter is open Monday to Friday 8:15 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The Library Office is open Monday to Saturday 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Library borrowing: undergraduate students can borrow 3 books for 15 days; postgraduate students and research scholars can borrow 4 books for 15 days; teaching faculty can borrow 8 books for a semester. Two renewals are allowed if nobody has reserved the book, and books can be renewed online through the library management system. A laptop can be borrowed for 14 days.

Library fines and rules: overdue charge is Rs. 1 per day for 1-15 days, Rs. 2 per day for 16-30 days and Rs. 5 per day from 31 days. Late return of a borrowed laptop costs Rs. 50 per day. Lost books must be replaced with a new copy plus overdue charges. Bags must be deposited at the entrance (only a small notebook or loose sheets are allowed inside), ID cards must be displayed, and misbehaviour can cancel membership. Library page: https://www.srmist.edu.in/library/

SRMIST runs air-conditioned buses from many parts of Chennai city to the Kattankulathur campus. You need a Bus Pass ID card, 2 passport-size photos and your ID number; booking and payment can be done online through the Student/Faculty Portal, subject to seat availability. The page lists the bus fee as Rs. 75,000, which is non-refundable and non-adjustable once paid. A duplicate bus pass costs Rs. 250.

Bus timings listed for Kattankulathur: Engineering and Technology buses reach campus at 7:40 AM and leave at 4:20 PM (Spell I), or arrive 8:30 AM and leave 5:15 PM (Spell II). Science and Humanities, Law and Management buses arrive at 7:50 AM and leave at 4:00 PM. Medical, Dental and Health Sciences buses arrive 7:50 AM and leave 4:10 PM. Transport office: 044-27417315, 044-27417316, 73388 28316, 89258 01548.

SRMIST student clubs listed on the official Clubs page include: Rotaract Club, Astrophilia (astronomy), Fashion, Music, Literature Club, Festival Club, Dance Club, Movies and Dramatics, Sports, Creative Arts and Media, Women Empowerment, Self Defense Club, Social Club, Gaming and Quiz Club. They cover music, dance, drama, art, literature, social service, sports and e-gaming. Page: https://www.srmist.edu.in/life-at-srm/student-life/clubs/

Technical clubs and chapters in the Department of Computing Technologies (CSE) include Coding Ninjas Club, Google Developer Group, Liftoff, E-Cell, SRMIST Quantum Computing Club, BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) Club, Cherry+ Network and FOSS Club.

Department of Computational Intelligence (CINTEL) student clubs include SRMKZILLA, NEXTGEN AI, TEDxSRMIST, the CINTEL Student Association and the IEI Students' Chapter. The Department of Networking and Communications hosts SRM Hackathon and SRM Ideathon and Semicolon, among other student bodies. Each department also lists its professional chapters and associations on its own 'Student Clubs' page.

Anti-ragging: SRMIST Anti-Ragging Helpline 9940036024 / 9940036028, email antiragging.helpline@srmist.edu.in. The National Anti-Ragging Helpline is 1800-180-5522 (24x7, toll free, helpline@antiragging.in). Ragging is a criminal offence; penalties can include cancellation of admission, suspension or expulsion, and incidents may be reported through an FIR. Official page: https://www.srmist.edu.in/life-at-srm/anti-ragging/

SRMIST scholarships (2023 onwards): Founder's Scholarship (4 years) for the top 100 SRMJEEE ranks, top 20,000 IIT JEE (Main) ranks, state or district toppers and exemplary sportspersons - renewal needs CGPA above 9. SRM Merit Scholarship for SRMJEEE ranks 101-500 - renewal needs CGPA above 9. You must usually apply every year before the deadline, with no arrears and no disciplinary action.

More SRMIST scholarships: Chancellor Constituency, Socio-Economic (low-income families; need-based requires parental income up to Rs. 6 lakh), Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, Differently-Abled and SRM Arts and Culture scholarships (renewal CGPA above 7); Employee Ward Scholarship (CGPA above 8, concession depends on parent's years of service); Alumni Scholarship (CGPA above 7); Performance Based Scholarship (CGPA above 9); Defence Scholarship for children of defence personnel (CGPA above 8). Full details: https://www.srmist.edu.in/policies/scholarship-policy/

Scholarships for other faculties: Medicine and Health Sciences - 100% waiver for scores of 98+ and 50% for 94-97; Management (MBA) - 100% for 98+, 50% for 94-97 and 25% for 90-93, renewal CGPA above 8; School of Law - 100% waiver for 98+, renewal CGPA above 8; Science and Humanities - 100% for 95+ percentile, renewal CGPA above 8. Scholarships are awarded on entrance-exam performance; attending counselling is usually mandatory.

SRMIST admission policy: the application fee for domestic candidates is Rs. 1,400 for Engineering and Technology programmes and Rs. 1,200 for all other programmes, paid online. Admission is merit based through SRM entrance exams (SRMJEEE, SRMJEEM, SRMJEEL and others) held in remote proctored online mode. Candidates with valid CUET scores are encouraged to apply to Science and Humanities, and valid CLAT scores are accepted for the 5-year Integrated Law programme.

Withdrawal and refund: cancellation of admission must be requested online only. The policy lists 31 August 2026 as the last date of withdrawal for Engineering, Management and MCA courses. Refunds follow UGC/AICTE guidelines, are processed within 30 working days if details are in order, and are paid only by RTGS/NEFT; requests after the stipulated period are not entertained. No change of course is allowed after the admission letter is issued. Hostel accommodation depends on availability and is allotted after tuition fees are paid.

Documents needed at enrolment include mark statements, transfer certificate and conduct certificate. Lateral entry depends on seat availability. Official admissions email: admissions.india@srmist.edu.in. SRMIST says it has not authorised any consultant, agency or agent for admissions, so apply only through https://www.srmist.edu.in and its Directorate of Admissions - beware of fake websites.

Management and Law admissions: MBA needs a bachelor's degree with at least 50% and admission is through SRMJEEM followed by a personal interview; valid CAT, XAT, MAT, GMAT, NMAT, CMAT or TANCET scores get direct consideration for the interview, and work experience is preferred. The 5-year Integrated Law programme uses the SRM entrance exam for law (SRMJEEL) or CLAT. Details: https://www.srmist.edu.in/admission-india/management/ and https://www.srmist.edu.in/admission-india/law/

Medicine and Health Sciences: UG programmes by entrance exam include BOT, BPT, B.Optom, B.Pharm, B.Sc. in Medical Imaging Technology, Medical Laboratory Technology, Nursing and Renal Dialysis Technology, BASLP and Pharm.D. PG programmes include M.OT, M.PT, M.Pharm (several specialisations), M.Sc. Nursing and M.Phil. Clinical Psychology; non-entrance PG options include MPH, MHA and several M.Sc. programmes. MBBS admission is through NEET: https://medical.srmist.edu.in/campaign/mbbs-md-ms-2026-27/

International admissions: NRI, PIO and OCI applicants can get a 40% fee waiver with SAT or a score of 70% and above in HSC grades. Foreign students from Africa, Asia and SAARC can get a 65% fee waiver in engineering and 50% in other programmes. NRI/PIO/OCI applicants use the international application form, not SRMJEEE. See https://www.srmist.edu.in/admission-international/

International Relations at SRMIST supports academic mobility, collaborative research, dual-degree programmes and international internships. The Semester Abroad Program lets students study a semester at partner universities; the International Relations office phone is +91 44 27417253. Details: https://www.srmist.edu.in/ir/outward-mobility/semester-abroad-program/ and https://www.srmist.edu.in/ir/global-partnerships/

Colleges at SRMIST Kattankulathur: Engineering and Technology, Medical and Health Sciences, Management, Science and Humanities (now called Liberal Arts and Business Studies), Hotel Management, Law and Agricultural Sciences, plus Distance Education (https://srmistdistanceeducation.in/) and Online Education (https://www.srmonline.in/).
